newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Irkutsk region plans more Eurobond issues.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Irkutsk region plans more Eurobond issues.

text.p: Russia's Irkutsk region is considering further Eurobonds after a debut issue at end 1997 or start 1998, an official with the agent, All-Russian Bank for Regional Development, said on Monday.
The Siberian region plans to issue about $80 million of dollar-denominated Eurobonds, planning department head Yevgeny Petrov told Reuters.

"It is obvious that for a serious investment jump in the region's development one issue is not enough," Petrov said. "$80 million is not enough for a serious rise in the region's economy. We are considering further borrowing within existing limits of the budget."
A draft law on regional Eurobond issues says a region cannot issue a Eurobond with a volume of more than 30 percent of its revenues, and debt servicing cannot exceed 15 percent of the revenues.
Petrov said the forthcoming Eurobond most likely would have a five-year tenor.
The region's administration will choose the lead manager in second half May, he said.
The Eurobond will be aimed mainly at Southeast Asian markets, such as Taiwan, Japan and South Korea.
The region plans to invest the proceeds in several projects under consideration.

They include development of the Kovyktinskoye natural gas field. According to some estimates, this holds confirmed reserves of 300 billion cubic meters and unconfirmed reserves of 600 billion cubic meters.
Several other Russian regions, including Nizhny Novgorod, the City of Moscow and the Moscow region, are lining up for Eurobonds.
The City of Moscow will hold a road-show May 11-23 in Asia, Europe and the United States.
